THESE PETITIONS COMING ON FOR ORDERS THIS DAY,
THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER 1.

In all these writ petitions, the awards that are passed by consent are called in question, with a direction to respondent No.3 to re-fix or re-determine the awards in accordance with the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013 ("the 2013 Act / new Act" for short) by awarding 100% solatium and payment of interest as sought for.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 2. A direction is also sought for to extend the benefit of rehabilitation and resettlement in accordance with the new Act and for a direction to respondent No.5 to refund the amount of tax deducted at source that had been deducted and deposited by respondent No.3 on behalf of the petitioners along with interest.

3. The principal contention advanced by the petitioners is that prior to the passing of these awards,
the Government had passed an order on 14.11.2014, by which all the earlier orders of the Government were superseded and a revised land acquisition, rehabilitation and resettlement principles and policy frame-work, including the Entitlement Matrix in respect of the land acquisition cases for rehabilitation and resettlement assistance to non-title holders, was detailed by way of an Annexure and was made applicable with immediate effect.

4. It is their case that since there was a Government Order laying down specific procedures to be followed in the matter of land acquisition and for the grant of compensation, it was necessary for the Authorities to apply the said Government Order and then pass the appropriate awards.

5. It is highlighted that the Government Order was issued taking note of the fact that the land acquisition process was in advanced stage and it had been decided to continue the process under the Karnataka Highways Act, 1964 by suitably amending the policy frame-work and Entitlement Matrix,
so as to ensure that the compensation and resettlement and rehabilitation are higher than the quantum prescribed under the 2013 Act.

sentences.text:
It is also contended that the provisions for land acquisition and compensation would have to be applied to all cases where the compensation awards or agreements have not been made as of 31.12.2013 as indicated in the Annexure and since admittedly, the awards or agreements were not made before 31.12.2013, it is obvious that the Government Order would have to apply.
7. Learned counsel also submits that since as per the Government Order, the intent of the State was to ensure that the land-losers are compensated in terms of the provisions of the 2013 Act, by virtue of Section 96 of the 2013 Act, there was an exemption for payment of the Income Tax and therefore,
it was necessary that the tax deducted at source by the authorities and deposited with the Income Tax Department should also be ordered to be refunded.
8.

Sri .C.V.Angadi, learned counsel for the Highways Authorities, on the other hand, contends that the compensation paid by way of agreement would have to prevail and the Government Order cannot be made applicable.
It is contended that the Government Order would not apply in cases where a consent award has already been passed.
9. It is not in dispute that in all these cases, the awards were passed after the Government Order dated 14.11.2014 was issued.

The Government Order dated 14.11.2014 came to be issued in order to ensure that the compensation and rehabilitation and resettlement assistance were provided to the land-losers which were equal or higher than the quantum prescribed under the 2013 Act.

10. Clause (1) of Annexure to the said Government Order clearly states that the provisions for compensation would be applied as per the Government Order to all cases where the awards or agreements had not been made before 31.12.2013.
11. It is therefore clear that the ultimate objective of this Government Order was to ensure that the land- losers get the compensation as provided under the 2013 Act.
12. Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the petitioners contends that they would be entitled to a higher sum of compensation if this Government Order is applied.

13. However, Sri.C.V.Angadi, learned counsel for the respondents, refutes this contention and contends that even if the compensation is re-worked as per the Government Order, the petitioners would not be getting a higher compensation.
14. For the purpose of these writ petitions, it would not be necessary to venture into this controversy.

15. Since the Government has stated its objective of ensuring compensation to the land-losers are provided as per the provisions of the 2013 Act, even in respect of the awards which had been passed after the 2013 Act came into force, it would be necessary to direct the concerned Authority to re-consider the matter by applying the Government Order dated 14.11.2014.

12 16.

entities.text: Meharwade Vishnu vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The competent authority shall notify the petitioners before re-considering the matter, afford an opportunity to the petitioners to have their say in the matter regarding the manner in which the 2014 order would have to be applied.
17. The petitioners are directed to be present before the concerned Authority on 05.06.2023 and the Authority shall re
-consider the entire matter and pass fresh awards in terms of this order.
18. It is made clear that if the petitioners are entitled for higher compensation pursuant to the reconsideration, the same shall be paid to them.
19. If however, it is found by the Authority that they are not entitled to a higher compensation, no steps shall be taken to seek for recovery of the amount that had already been paid.

20. As far as contention regarding deduction of the tax deducted at source is concerned, as noticed above, the Government intended to apply the provisions of the 2013 Act, in relation to the compensation that became payable after the 2013 Act came into force.
21. Admittedly, in the instant case, the award was passed after the 2013 Act come into force.

It is therefore clear that Section 96 of the 2013 Act would have to be applied and consequentially, the land-losers would be exempted from payment of income tax in respect of the compensation payable to them.
22.

Since, it is contended that the tax has been deducted at source as per the then prevailing law when the 2013 Act was not applied, the Income Tax Department is directed to refund the tax that has been deposited to the account of the petitioners within a period of two months from today.
23. It would be for the Income Tax Department to proceed against the Government and seek for income tax if they are so entitled, in accordance with law.
24. The Writ Petitions are allowed accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
In all these writ petitions, the awards that are passed by consent are called in question, with a direction to respondent No.3 to re-fix or re-determine the awards in accordance with the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013 ("the 2013 Act / new Act" for short) by awarding 100% solatium and payment of interest as sought for.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Shri. Meharwade Vishnu vs State Of Karnataka on 12 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145201393/
11 6.
It is also contended that the provisions for land acquisition and compensation would have to be applied to all cases where the compensation awards or agreements have not been made as of 31.12.2013 as indicated in the Annexure and since admittedly, the awards or agreements were not made before 31.12.2013, it is obvious that the Government Order would have to apply.
7. Learned counsel also submits that since as per the Government Order, the intent of the State was to ensure that the land-losers are compensated in terms of the provisions of the 2013 Act, by virtue of Section 96 of the 2013 Act, there was an exemption for payment of the Income Tax and therefore,
it was necessary that the tax deducted at source by the authorities and deposited with the Income Tax Department should also be ordered to be refunded.
8.
10. Clause (1) of Annexure to the said Government Order clearly states that the provisions for compensation would be applied as per the Government Order to all cases where the awards or agreements had not been made before 31.12.2013.
11. It is therefore clear that the ultimate objective of this Government Order was to ensure that the land- losers get the compensation as provided under the 2013 Act.
13. However, Sri.C.V.Angadi, learned counsel for the respondents, refutes this contention and contends that even if the compensation is re-worked as per the Government Order, the petitioners would not be getting a higher compensation.
opennyai_summary.decision:
The competent authority shall notify the petitioners before re-considering the matter, afford an opportunity to the petitioners to have their say in the matter regarding the manner in which the 2014 order would have to be applied.
17. The petitioners are directed to be present before the concerned Authority on 05.06.2023 and the Authority shall re
-consider the entire matter and pass fresh awards in terms of this order.
18. It is made clear that if the petitioners are entitled for higher compensation pursuant to the reconsideration, the same shall be paid to them.
23. It would be for the Income Tax Department to proceed against the Government and seek for income tax if they are so entitled, in accordance with law.
24. The Writ Petitions are allowed accordingly.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
21. Admittedly, in the instant case, the award was passed after the 2013 Act come into force.
It is therefore clear that Section 96 of the 2013 Act would have to be applied and consequentially, the land-losers would be exempted from payment of income tax in respect of the compensation payable to them.
22.
Since, it is contended that the tax has been deducted at source as per the then prevailing law when the 2013 Act was not applied, the Income Tax Department is directed to refund the tax that has been deposited to the account of the petitioners within a period of two months from today.
